legalRules.title: Definition of Record
legalRules.proposition: In this synthetic instrument, 'record' means a stored notice and its receipt timestamp.

legalRules.title: Applicability to Operators Offering Public Notice Service
legalRules.proposition: This instrument applies only to operators offering the notice service to the public. Private household use is outside this scope.

legalRules.title: Exception for Temporary Test Records
legalRules.proposition: The retention duty in Article 5 does not apply to a temporary test record.

legalRules.title: Receipt Timestamp Timing
legalRules.proposition: A receipt timestamp is recorded when the notice is received, not when it is drafted. The receipt timestamp begins the retention period.

legalRules.title: Seven-Day Retention Duty
legalRules.proposition: An operator within Article 2 must retain each record for 7 days, subject to Article 3.
applicabilityConditions: The operator must be offering the notice service to the public (not private household use)
exceptions: Does not apply to temporary test records

legalRules.title: Retention of Notice Text with Timestamp
legalRules.proposition: Keep the notice text with its receipt timestamp.
applicabilityConditions: The operator must be offering the notice service to the public (not private household use)
exceptions: Does not apply to temporary test records

legalRules.title: Preservation Without Removing Limiting Language
legalRules.proposition: Preserve the notice text without removing its limiting language.
applicabilityConditions: The operator must be offering the notice service to the public (not private household use)
exceptions: Does not apply to temporary test records

legalRules.title: Appointment for Annual Public Information Session
legalRules.proposition: The operator must appoint a person to attend the annual public information session in person. Attendance is recorded in the session register maintained by the organizer.
applicabilityConditions: The operator must be offering the notice service to the public (not private household use)

coverage.nonAssessableReason: This duty requires in-person attendance at an annual session and appointment of a person, which cannot be assessed through repository analysis. The attendance is recorded in an external session register maintained by a separate organizer.

engineeringRules.legalIntent: Ensure that the system recognizes and implements the definition of 'record' as a stored notice with its receipt timestamp.
engineeringRules.applicabilityGuidance: Applies to any system component that creates, stores, or processes records as defined by the legal instrument.

criteria.statement: The system must store notices together with their receipt timestamps as a unified record structure.

investigationGoals: Identify data structures, classes, or database schemas that represent notices
Verify that receipt timestamps are stored alongside notice content
edgeStrategies: Follow HAS_FIELD, HAS_PROPERTY, HAS_COLUMN edges from notice-related types
patterns: Data structures containing both notice content and timestamp fields
Classes or types named Record, Notice, or similar with timestamp properties
requiredEvidence: Data structure definition showing notice content field and receipt timestamp field stored together
supportingEvidence: Database schema with notice and timestamp columns in same table
Constructor or factory methods that initialize both fields together
Documentation or comments explaining the record structure
negativeEvidence: Timestamp stored separately from notice content

engineeringRules.legalIntent: Determine whether the system is offered to the public (in scope) or is for private household use (out of scope).
engineeringRules.applicabilityGuidance: This rule helps establish whether the legal obligations apply to the system under assessment.

criteria.statement: The system must be identifiable as either offering notice service to the public or being for private household use.

User registration or authentication for external users
requiredEvidence: Configuration or documentation indicating the service is offered to the public
supportingEvidence: Terms of service or user agreements for public users

engineeringRules.legalIntent: Identify which records are temporary test records (exempt from retention) versus production records (subject to retention).
engineeringRules.applicabilityGuidance: Applies to systems that distinguish between test and production data.

criteria.statement: The system must be able to identify or distinguish temporary test records from production records.

investigationGoals: Find flags, markers, or separate storage for test records

Check configuration for test mode settings

requiredEvidence: Mechanism to identify or flag records as temporary test records
supportingEvidence: Code that handles test records differently from production records

engineeringRules.legalIntent: Ensure the receipt timestamp is recorded when the notice is received by the system, not when it is drafted or created by the sender.
engineeringRules.applicabilityGuidance: Applies to any code path that receives and processes incoming notices.

criteria.statement: The system must record the receipt timestamp at the point when the notice is received, not using a timestamp from the notice content or creation time.

investigationGoals: Identify where notices are received (API endpoints, message handlers, etc.)
Verify that timestamps are generated at reception time
Ensure timestamps are not copied from incoming message metadata
edgeStrategies: Follow CALLS edges to timestamp generation functions
Look for timestamp assignment in receive handlers
Trace data flow from reception point to storage
patterns: Timestamp generated using current time APIs at reception
Timestamp assignment in message receive handlers
requiredEvidence: Code that generates current timestamp when notice is received
supportingEvidence: API endpoint or message handler that assigns receipt timestamp
Comments or documentation explaining timestamp recording at reception
Rejection or overwriting of client-provided timestamps
negativeEvidence: Using timestamp from incoming message payload as receipt timestamp
Recording timestamp at notice draft/creation time instead of reception

engineeringRules.legalIntent: Ensure that each record (notice with receipt timestamp) is retained for at least 7 days from the receipt timestamp, except for temporary test records.
engineeringRules.applicabilityGuidance: Applies to all production records; does not apply to temporary test records.

criteria.statement: Production records must be retained for at least 7 days from their receipt timestamp.
The retention period must begin from the receipt timestamp, not from any other date.
Temporary test records may be excluded from the 7-day retention requirement.

investigationGoals: Identify record deletion, archival, or cleanup logic
Verify retention period is at least 7 days

Check that test records are handled separately if applicable
edgeStrategies: Look for scheduled tasks that purge old records

Retention policies configured to 7 days or more
TTL (time-to-live) settings of at least 7 days
Deletion logic that checks age against receipt timestamp
requiredEvidence: Retention period of at least 7 days from receipt timestamp
Logic that preserves records for the required duration
supportingEvidence: Configuration files with retention settings >= 7 days
Scheduled tasks that run no more frequently than every 7 days for cleanup
Database TTL or expiration settings >= 7 days
negativeEvidence: Deletion based on creation time rather than receipt timestamp

engineeringRules.legalIntent: Ensure that stored notice text is preserved without removing or modifying its limiting language or qualifiers.
engineeringRules.applicabilityGuidance: Applies to all stored production notices (except temporary test records).

criteria.statement: Notice text must be stored without modification that would remove limiting language.
The system must not strip, sanitize, or transform notice content in ways that alter limiting language, qualifiers, or conditions.

investigationGoals: Identify text processing, sanitization, or transformation logic

Examine sanitization, validation, or transformation logic
patterns: Notice text stored verbatim without content modification

requiredEvidence: Notice text stored without content-altering transformations
Code showing verbatim or safe storage of notice content
